title: Testing and GitHub Pages
text:
composer install
composer validate --strict
composer lint
composer test
export CMDSTAN=/absolute/path/to/cmdstan-2.40.0
composer test:integration
composer test:compatibility   # additionally needs R + cmdstanr, posterior, loo, bayesplot, jsonlite, Rcpp, RcppEigen
The unit suite does not need CmdStan. Moment-matching tests also need the phit extension with its posterior-draw kernels (for example php -d extension=/path/to/libphit.dylib vendor/bin/phpunit) and skip without it. It verifies JSON shapes and invalid data, CSV comments/warmup/special numbers, draw layouts, summaries, diagnostics, serialization, option validation, process argument isolation, pipe draining, timeouts, cancellation, and bounded execution. It uses real PHP subprocesses for process behavior. Data frame interoperability is tested with stand-in tables and a stand-in Phibble\DataFrame, so phibble is not needed. Without phit, StanData::fromFormula() is tested with a stand-in Phit\model_matrix(). With it, the tests cover random intercepts and slopes, factor predictors and responses, and dropped rows against the real function.
The integration suite compiles the bundled models and invokes real CmdStan methods. It compares Bernoulli posterior estimates with their analytic mean, checks R-hat and ESS, verifies deterministic seeds with parallel chains, confirms modes and draw counts, and exercises generated quantities, fixed parameters, syntax/formatting, gradient checking, log density, input errors, metrics, and auxiliary files. It fits a hierarchical regression built with StanData::fromColumns(), runs a model on table data, and, when phit is loaded, fits score ~ study_hours + (1 | school) built with StanData::fromFormula() on phit’s schools data and compares the posterior means with Phit\fit_lmer(). It also builds FFI libraries for model methods and exposed functions, initializes chains from fits, runs the example models, and computes LOO with and without moment matching. Tests that need FFI skip when it is unavailable. If CmdStan is not available, PHPUnit skips these tests; CI explicitly installs CmdStan so they execute there.
Tests use small models and a modest number of draws. They do not constitute a full upstream CmdStanR conformance suite, do not test a real MPI cluster or OpenCL hardware, and do not establish native Windows support. The package’s compatibility contract lists remaining gaps.
The compatibility suite runs the same algorithms with CmdStanR and PHP using identical seeds and precision, then compares individual parameter/log-density draws, approximate densities, descriptive summaries, R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, and MCMC diagnostics. MCMC comparisons include even and odd chain lengths. Further comparisons cover CSV metadata keys, in-process log densities, gradients, Hessians, constrain/unconstrain results, exposed Stan functions, PSIS, LOO, LOO moment matching, WAIC, relative efficiency, and posterior summary measures. Moment matching is compared with loo::loo_moment_match.default() on analytic regression posteriors, both unmodified and with loo’s split step corrected as documented, and with CmdStanR’s loo(moment_match = TRUE) on a same-seed fit. The values behind the figures are compared with R and bayesplot. R, CmdStanR, posterior, loo, bayesplot, jsonlite, Rcpp, and RcppEigen are needed. These tests skip when their prerequisites are absent.
The moment-matching reference was verified with CmdStanR 0.9.0 and two loo 2.10.1.9000 development builds: 7991145, from before stan-dev/loo#405, and fd910fe, which includes it. The isolated R reference in tests/fixtures/moment_match.R records the loo version and commit and contains the explicit split-inverse and two-half efficiency corrections. With an earlier loo, the suite checks that loo’s own split differs where a shift is combined with scaling or a covariance map. With a corrected loo, it checks that loo’s own split matches CmdStanPHP for every design. Transform-order preservation also has an independent regression test.

title: Testing and GitHub Pages
text:
Continuous integration
.github/workflows/tests.yml runs unit tests on PHP 8.2, 8.3, and 8.4. A separate integration matrix builds CmdStan 2.37 and 2.40 on Linux, runs the real-model suite, and caches each toolchain. The integration jobs enable PHP’s FFI extension and render every figure kind to SVG, and one to PNG, with a downloaded vl-convert binary. The 2.40 job additionally installs the reference R packages and runs the compatibility suite. Installation is performed using this package’s installer to exercise its download/build path. Compilation on small CI machines is memory-intensive; integration uses two make jobs.
The integration jobs build phit from the pinned phpstats/phit commit b71e406ee58fc7a255687514b2818c3c615a517b, which adds Phit\model_matrix() and Phit\fit_lmer() (the draw kernels and Phit\dist_normal_rng() are unchanged since e7457cb), using PHP 8.4 headers to match the runner. They require all three draw kernels, FFI, the seeded draw generator, Phit\model_matrix(), and Phit\fit_lmer() before running native unit tests (including StanData::fromFormula() against the real function), real-model tests, and (on CmdStan 2.40) R comparisons. These runs fail on skipped tests. The real-model run excludes the compatibility group until R is installed. The lightweight unit matrix still tests the optional-extension path without phit. Local native tests must likewise use a PHP executable matching the extension module ABI; a Homebrew PHP 8.5 extension cannot load into Herd PHP 8.4.

title: Testing and GitHub Pages
text:
Documentation site
All site content is under docs/, written in Quarto. Each page is a .qmd source with its rendered .html committed beside it, which is also the layout the phpstats.org site reads when it imports a package’s documentation. No page executes code, so rendering needs neither CmdStan nor a Stan toolchain.
To render the site after editing a page:
quarto render docs
rsync -a --exclude '.DS_Store' docs/_site/ docs/
Quarto writes the rendered site to the untracked docs/_site, and the second command publishes it beside the sources. Both commands are needed. The render step deletes the published pages and site_libs/ from docs/, so running it without the rsync leaves the rendered site staged only under docs/_site. Commit the regenerated .html files along with search.json, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and site_libs/ whenever a source page changes. To preview while editing, run quarto preview docs.
Links between pages are written as relative .qmd targets, which Quarto renders as relative .html links. The site therefore works at a domain root, at a repository subpath, and when phpstats.org imports the rendered pages.
.github/workflows/pages.yml checks the committed site’s internal links with scripts/check-docs.py on pull requests and on main, so a broken link is caught before publication. These checks run even before GitHub Pages is enabled. A separate job publishes docs/ from main or a manual dispatch on main. Deployment uses GitHub’s Pages artifact and environment; no token beyond GITHUB_TOKEN is needed.
After pushing this repository through your normal workflow, select Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions. The workflow then handles the publication. Repository settings cannot be enabled by writing files alone, and no remote publication has been performed in this workspace.

Figures
$density = CmdStan\mcmc_dens($fit, 'theta');
echo $density->ascii(60, 10), "\n";
echo CmdStan\mcmc_intervals($fit)->ascii(60), "\n";
file_put_contents('theta.html', $density->html());
$spec = $density->vegaLite(width: 480, height: 240);

  |               ********
  |             ***      ***
  |            **          **
  |           **            ***
2 +          **               **
  |         **                 ****
  |        **                     ***
  |      ***                        ****
  |     **                             *******
0 +******                                    ******************
  +----+--------------------------------+----------------------
       0                               0.5
   theta (y: density)

intervals: 50% inner, 90% outer, point = median
theta |-----------[=========o==========]--------------------
      +-----------------+--------------------------+--------
                       0.2                        0.4
       - outer, [=] inner, o = median
The figure functions follow bayesplot’s names and return a Figure. A figure holds the computed statistics in data, as documented on the Figure class, and renders them in several forms:

ascii(width, height) returns plain ASCII text for a terminal, log, or text report. Echoing a figure prints this form with default sizes.
vegaLite(width, height, maxRows) returns a Vega-Lite 5 spec as a PHP array with the data inlined, and json() returns the same spec as JSON that is safe to place in an HTML script element. Front ends render it with vega-embed or any other Vega-Lite runtime.
html() returns a standalone page that loads Vega, Vega-Lite, and vega-embed from the jsDelivr CDN.
svg() and png(scale: 2.0) render static images with vl-convert, a standalone binary that needs no Node or browser. Set VL_CONVERT to its path or put vl-convert on PATH.

The available figures are:

mcmc_trace($fit, 'theta'): chains overlaid by iteration.
mcmc_hist($fit, 'theta', bins: 30): histogram of all draws.
mcmc_dens($fit, 'theta') and mcmc_dens_overlay($fit, 'theta'): Gaussian kernel density of all draws, or one curve per chain.
mcmc_intervals($fit, ['mu', 'beta'], prob: 0.5, probOuter: 0.9, pointEst: 'median'): inner and outer intervals with a point estimate on a shared axis. Without a selection it plots every variable except lp__.
mcmc_rank_hist($fit, 'theta', bins: 20): per-chain histograms of pooled ranks, with the count expected under uniform ranks marked.
mcmc_scatter($fit, 'mu', 'sigma'): joint draws, with divergent transitions marked on MCMC fits.
mcmc_acf($fit, 'theta', lags: 20): per-chain autocorrelation bars.
pareto_k_plot($fit->loo()): Pareto k by observation, with the k threshold and k = 1 marked.

A plotted variable names one element, such as beta[2]. mcmc_intervals() also accepts base names, which select every element. The functions take a fit or a draws_array.
The bandwidth (R’s bw.nrd0), densities, quantiles, ranks, and autocorrelations are computed in PHP and checked against R and bayesplot. Vega-Lite specs carry these values and use no Vega-Lite density, binning, or quantile transforms, so every rendering shows the same numbers. The ASCII form rounds positions to character cells; use the figure’s data or the numeric methods, such as summary(), when exact values matter.
Trace and scatter figures inline every draw. For large fits, maxRows keeps every k-th iteration of a trace, or every k-th draw of a scatter plus all divergent draws, so that about that many rows remain. Per-chain figures (rank histograms and autocorrelation) are faceted by chain, and their sizes apply to each chain’s panel.

title: Inference guide
Compatibility contract
text: This package ports CmdStanR’s core model/executable/CSV workflow to PHP. It does not claim full CmdStanR compatibility. The reference is the CmdStanR API and CmdStan CLI, consulted during implementation. PHP interfaces preserve modern option names wherever their meaning transfers directly. Method names do not carry over: PSR-1 makes a PHP method name camelCase, so CmdStanR’s fit$output_files() is $fit->outputFiles() here. The method names table maps every one of them, and the package declares no snake_case alias beside the camelCase name.

title: Compatibility contract
text:
PHP adaptations
R named lists become associative PHP arrays; numeric arrays must be rectangular zero-indexed lists. R sparse matrices, complex numbers, NA, and automatic R object conversion have no PHP equivalent. Data frames and factors can come from phibble or any object with toModelData() or toColumns(), following the conventions in the API reference. code() returns one source string. Syntax errors throw exceptions rather than returning an R diagnostic list.
R posterior objects become PHP arrays with documented shapes. All array indices are zero-based; draw metadata is one-based. draws_array retains iteration/chain axes, draws_matrix concatenates chains, draws_df is associative rows, draws_list maps variables to values per chain, and draws_rvars nests each variable’s draws by its dimensions. R tibble, posterior, bayesplot, and ggplot2 classes are not emulated. The default draws format follows CmdStanR: draws_array for MCMC and generated quantities and draws_matrix for other methods.
Summary quantiles use linear interpolation (R’s default type 7). Scaled MAD uses 1.4826. The default MCMC summary delegates R-hat and bulk ESS to the installed CmdStan stansummary and computes tail ESS in PHP. Passing measures to summary() uses a PHP port of posterior’s summarise_draws(), including rank-normalized R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, and MCSE, so it does not need CmdStan. Results are checked against the installed reference R packages, but are not guaranteed bit-for-bit identical to every version of posterior. ADVI’s mean row is stored separately. ADVI and Laplace log_p__ columns are normalized to lp__ and their approximate densities to lp_approx__, matching CmdStanR. Non-MCMC convergence statistics are NAN.
metadata() returns one merged array with CmdStanR’s keys, such as iter_sampling, max_treedepth, and stan_variable_sizes, alongside CmdStan’s raw argument names. chainMetadata() returns the per-chain arrays. invMetric() returns matrices by default and reads metric JSON when every chain has one.
Model methods and exposed functions compile a shared library against the selected CmdStan and load it with PHP FFI. FFI is enabled for the CLI by default (ffi.enable=preload); web SAPIs need ffi.enable=true or preloading. Libraries are cached beside the Stan source with a fingerprint in the file name. Model methods drop constant terms and default to jacobian: true, as in CmdStanR. Unconstrained vectors are flat lists, and constrained variables are nested zero-based arrays with matrices as lists of rows. Fits serialize the library path, data, and seed, and reconnect on first use; the generated-quantities RNG then restarts from its seed.
Initialization from a fit follows CmdStanR’s process_init(). MCMC draws are resampled without replacement, an optimization estimate is repeated, and ADVI, Laplace, and Pathfinder draws are resampled with Pareto-smoothed importance weights. Resampling uses PHP’s seeded Mt19937 engine, so a given seed selects different draws than CmdStanR does.
Diagnostic checks are structured messages accessible with diagnosticWarnings(), rather than PHP runtime warnings. Console output is buffered; there is no R progress-bar or interrupt integration. show_messages controls stdout, show_exceptions controls stderr. Deprecated CmdStanR argument names raise E_USER_DEPRECATED and map to their replacements; conflicting old and new values throw. Output files persist after garbage collection, so callers manage cleanup explicitly. Saving moves files that a run created and copies imported CSVs and user-supplied data files; existing destinations are never overwritten. Saved fit objects use PHP serialization and embed parsed results; CSVs are still needed for downstream CmdStan commands.
options() and cmdstan_option() provide CmdStanR’s global options that have a PHP meaning: default output directory, Stan file directory, forced recompilation, draws format, initialization warnings, verbose compilation, printed rows, line numbers, and mc.cores. cmdstanr_no_ver_check is accepted and has no effect because this package never checks for updates.
Algorithm parameters left null use CmdStan’s defaults. PHP-level defaults include four sample chains, sequential execution unless requested, and one MPI chain. CmdStanR defaults for automatically saving metric/configuration JSON are not imposed; request save_metric or save_cmdstan_config explicitly. The installer defaults to one core where CmdStanR uses two. OpenCL and MPI require external toolchains/hardware. Windows has not been validated.
Moment matching follows loo::loo_moment_match() as CmdStanMCMC$loo() calls it, with corrections to the split step and relative efficiencies. loo’s development version adopted the split corrections in stan-dev/loo#405 on 2026-10-13; the differences below are from loo 2.10.1 and earlier development builds. The split uses the exact inverse of the accumulated affine map, where loo subtracts the shift after the inverse linear map. The split relative efficiency is the minimum over both halves, where loo uses the second half twice. Relative efficiencies use exp(log_lik − max), which avoids the NA that loo returns when every likelihood value is tiny. Without the split, and with the split when only shifts are accepted, elpd_loo and Pareto k match loo and CmdStanR. Accepted scale and covariance steps are composed in their original order, including cases where scaling follows a covariance map. A singular weighted covariance uses loo’s identity-map fallback while retaining the mean shift; its reason is recorded in covariance_fallbacks. Other numerical or model failures stop the observation at its last accepted state and record a reason. Covariances are never regularized. The inference guide describes the result.

title: Compatibility contract
text:
Not implemented
The following CmdStanR features have no implementation:

expose_functions(global = TRUE). Functions are called as methods of the returned StanFunctions object. Functions ending in _lp and overloaded functions are listed but cannot be called.
bayesplot’s other plots, including pairs, areas, NUTS energy, and posterior predictive checks. Figures are not ggplot2 objects and cannot be extended with ggplot2 layers or themes.
Posterior rvar arithmetic and R session hooks beyond the options listed above.
Windows toolchain repair (check_cmdstan_toolchain(fix = TRUE)). The PHP toolchain check reports missing tools and does not install them.
Parity with every CmdStanR version’s error and warning messages.

No unsupported option is accepted silently. This repository’s tests validate the implemented contract against the installed CmdStanR, posterior, and loo packages; they are not the upstream CmdStanR test suite. Direct conformance tests run CmdStanR and PHP with the same seeds and compare draws, descriptive summaries, MCMC sampler diagnostics, CSV metadata, model methods, exposed functions, PSIS, LOO, WAIC, and posterior summary measures.

title: API reference
text: All classes and functions are in the CmdStan namespace. Standalone functions keep CmdStanR’s snake_case spelling. Methods, parameters, and properties are camelCase, as PSR-1 and this family’s conventions require, so CmdStanR’s fit$output_files() is $fit->outputFiles(); the compatibility contract maps every renamed method. CmdStan option names are unchanged. Inference methods accept PHP named arguments or one associative options array; they reject unknown options instead of silently ignoring them. null generally leaves the installed CmdStan default in effect. Check the compatibility contract for exceptions.

title: API reference
text:
Functions







Function
Purpose

Construct and optionally compile a model

Select/read CmdStan installation


cmdstan_version()
Read installed release version


check_cmdstan_toolchain()
Return paths and versions of make, CmdStan’s C++ compiler, and stanc; throws when make or the compiler is missing. It does not prove a compilation will succeed


install_cmdstan(version: null, dir: null, cores: null, timeout: null, overwrite: false, releaseUrl: null, releaseFile: null, cppOptions: [], checkToolchain: true)
Download or unpack and build a release (see the installation guide)


cmdstan_make_local(dir: null, cppOptions: [], append: true)
Read or write CmdStan’s make/local


rebuild_cmdstan(cores: null, timeout: null)
Clean and rebuild selected CmdStan


options(set: []) / cmdstan_option(name, default: null)
Set global options, returning previous values, or read one option


write_stan_file(code, file: null, dir: null, basename: null, forceOverwrite: false, hashSalt: '')
Write Stan source to model_<hash>.stan, reusing identical files


write_stan_json(data, file)
Write numeric data/initialization/metric JSON; data may also be a StanData or a table


read_cmdstan_csv(files) / as_cmdstan_fit(files)
Import one or more CmdStan CSV files into a typed fit


read_cmdstan_csv_list(files, variables: null, samplerDiagnostics: null, format: null)
Return CmdStanR’s read_cmdstan_csv() list shape


draws_to_csv(chains, dir)
Export [chain][iteration][variable] associative draw rows to separate CSV files


mcmc_trace, mcmc_hist, mcmc_dens, mcmc_dens_overlay, mcmc_intervals, mcmc_rank_hist, mcmc_scatter, mcmc_acf, pareto_k_plot
Return a Figure named after its bayesplot or loo counterpart; see the inference guide


cmdstanr_example(example: 'logistic', method: 'sample', ...options) / print_example_program(example)
Run or print the logistic, schools, or schools_ncp example



read_sample_csv(), write_stan_tempfile(), and num_threads() remain as deprecated CmdStanR names.

Global options
options() accepts cmdstanr_output_dir, cmdstanr_write_stan_file_dir, cmdstanr_force_recompile, cmdstanr_draws_format, cmdstanr_warn_inits, cmdstanr_verbose, cmdstanr_no_ver_check, cmdstanr_max_rows, cmdstanr_print_line_numbers, mc.cores, and cmdstanphp_example_dir. A null value unsets an option. Unknown names and values of the wrong type throw. mc.cores sets the default parallel_chains and installer core count.
Data arrays use named PHP arrays at the top level and zero-indexed lists for Stan arrays, vectors, and matrices. Boolean values become 0/1. Matrices are rows of rows, with no R column-major conversion. Empty top-level data becomes {}. Missing values, strings, objects, nonfinite numbers, sparse indices, invalid variable names, and ragged arrays are rejected.

title: API reference
text:
Model methods
stanFile(), exeFile(), hppFile(), and code() return paths or source text. exposeFunctions(timeout: null) compiles the model’s user-defined functions and returns a StanFunctions object; functions() returns it afterwards. modelName(), hasStanFile(), cppOptions(), and includePaths() expose model identity and recorded compiler settings. print(lineNumbers: false) writes source to stdout. saveHppFile(dir) copies the generated header. variables() returns stanc’s JSON information for source-level declarations and dimensions. format(overwriteFile: false, stancOptions: []) returns formatted Stan and optionally overwrites the source. checkSyntax(stancOptions: []) throws on invalid Stan and returns true on success.
compile(forceRecompile: null, stancOptions: [], cppOptions: [], cores: 1, timeout: null) compiles via CmdStan’s makefile and returns the model. Compiler options use associative arrays, e.g. ['warn-pedantic' => true] or ['STAN_THREADS' => true]. Make values containing command expansions or shell metacharacters are rejected. stanc option values with whitespace are not supported. Changing options removes stale model artifacts before rebuilding.








Method
Fit type
Required CmdStan




sample() / sampleMpi()
CmdStanMCMC
2.31+ supported baseline


optimize()
CmdStanMLE
2.31+


variational()
CmdStanVB
2.31+


pathfinder()

2.33+

The CI version targets are 2.37 and 2.40. Availability of individual options remains determined by the selected CmdStan; options added in newer releases can fail on older releases with CmdStan’s error message.

Shared options
data, seed, refresh, init, output_dir, output_basename, sig_figs, threads, threads_per_chain, num_threads, opencl_ids, show_messages, show_exceptions, save_latent_dynamics, save_cmdstan_config, timeout.
init additionally accepts a fit object (see the inference guide). Deprecated CmdStanR names are mapped with an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice: on sample(), cores, num_cores, num_chains, num_warmup, num_samples, max_depth, stepsize, save_extra_diagnostics, and validate_csv; on optimize(), laplace(), and logProb(), jacobian_adjustment.
Thread options are aliases, with precedence threads_per_chain, threads, then num_threads. Prefer the argument appropriate to the method. sig_figs is 1–18. opencl_ids contains platform/device IDs and requires an OpenCL build. output_basename contains only letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens. save_latent_dynamics creates auxiliary diagnostic CSVs; these may be empty for some algorithms. save_cmdstan_config requests CmdStan configuration JSON beside the CSVs.


Method-specific options

sample: chains (default 4), parallel_chains (default 1), chain_ids, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, save_warmup, thin, max_treedepth, adapt_engaged, adapt_delta, step_size, metric, metric_file, inv_metric, init_buffer, term_buffer, window, fixed_param, save_metric, diagnostics.
optimize: algorithm, jacobian, init_alpha, iter, tol_obj, tol_rel_obj, tol_grad, tol_rel_grad, tol_param, history_size, save_iterations.
variational: algorithm, iter, grad_samples, elbo_samples, eta, adapt_engaged, adapt_iter, tol_rel_obj, eval_elbo, output_samples, draws (alias for output_samples).
pathfinder: init_alpha, tol_obj, tol_rel_obj, tol_grad, tol_rel_grad, tol_param, history_size, single_path_draws, draws, num_paths, max_lbfgs_iters, num_elbo_draws, save_single_paths, psis_resample, calculate_lp.
laplace: mode, opt_args, jacobian (default true), draws, calculate_lp.
generate_quantities: required fittedParams is a fit, filename, or filename list; parallel_chains controls concurrency.
diagnose: epsilon, error for finite-difference gradient checks.
log_prob: exactly one of unconstrained_params, constrained_params, and optional jacobian.

sampleMpi(mpiCmd: 'mpiexec', mpiArgs: [], ...options) accepts sampling options, defaults to one chain, and executes chains sequentially. An associative MPI argument such as ['n' => 4] becomes -n 4; a list is passed as a literal argument vector. Compile with ['STAN_MPI' => true, 'CXX' => 'mpicxx', 'TBB_CXX_TYPE' => 'gcc'] and install an MPI runtime. MPI launch construction is unit-tested; a real MPI cluster run is not validated here.

title: API reference
text:
Fit methods

draws(variables: null, format: null, incWarmup: false): select posterior variables. Formats are draws_array, draws_matrix, draws_df, draws_list, and draws_rvars; null uses the cmdstanr_draws_format option or the method default.
samplerDiagnostics(format: null, incWarmup: false): diagnostic columns ending in __, excluding lp__.
summary(variables: null, probs: [0.05, 0.95], measures: []): descriptive and MCMC convergence summaries, or the requested summary measures.
diagnosticSummary(): per-chain num_divergent, num_max_treedepth, and ebfmi arrays.
checkDiagnostics(checks: ['divergences', 'treedepth', 'ebfmi']), diagnosticWarnings(): check and read messages.
cmdstanDiagnose(): invoke CmdStan’s diagnostic utility and return text.
metadata(), chainMetadata(), variables(), numChains(), numDrawsSampling(), numDrawsWarmup(): inspect parsed CSV.
stepSize(), invMetric(matrix: true): adaptation results, one entry per chain.
time(): per-chain warmup, sampling, and total time when available.
output(), returnCodes(): captured console output and process status. Imported fits have no process logs or status codes.
outputFiles(), latentDynamicsFiles(), profileFiles(), profiles(): output paths and parsed profiling data. The file accessors accept includeFailed for CmdStanR compatibility; fits only contain successful runs. Latent-dynamics and profile accessors throw when no such files exist.
dataFile(), configFiles(), metricFiles(), cmdstanConfig(), metric(): data and auxiliary JSON paths and their decoded contents. Imported fits use the data file recorded in the CSV when it still exists.
code(), numProcs(), lp(), cmdstanSummary(): stored source, number of processes, log-density matrix, and native text summary. Imported CSV fits do not include source code.
saveOutputFiles(), saveLatentDynamicsFiles(), saveProfileFiles(), saveDataFile(), saveConfigFiles(), saveMetricFiles(): each takes dir: '.', basename: null, timestamp: true, random: true and names files basename-YYYYmmddHHMM-id-xxxxxx.ext as CmdStanR does. Files created by the run are moved; imported and user-supplied files are copied. Existing destinations are never overwritten.
saveObject(file): serialize parsed fit data (and native MCMC summary statistics) to a PHP object file.
print(variables: null, maxRows: null): emit summary JSON to stdout, limited to cmdstanr_max_rows (default 10) variables.
drawsColumns(), summaryColumns(), drawsTable(), summaryTable(): column-oriented draws and summaries for data frames; see data frames.


Model methods
These methods need PHP FFI. The first call compiles a shared library for the fit’s model and data; initModelMethods(seed: 1, verbose: false, hessian: false, model: null) does this explicitly. Imported CSV fits must pass model:.

logProb(unconstrainedVariables, jacobian: true): log density with constants dropped.
gradLogProb(...): ['log_prob' => float, 'gradient' => list].
hessian(...): ['log_prob' => float, 'grad_log_prob' => list, 'hessian' => rows].
unconstrainVariables(variables): a flat unconstrained list from parameter values keyed by name.
unconstrainDraws(files: null, draws: null, format: null, incWarmup: false): the fit’s draws, another set of CSV files, or draws_df rows, in unconstrained space.
constrainVariables(unconstrainedVariables, transformedParameters: true, generatedQuantities: true): variables keyed by name as nested arrays.
variableSkeleton(transformedParameters: true, generatedQuantities: true): variable name to dimension list.
exposeFunctions(timeout: null) / functions(): the model’s user-defined functions.

jacobianAdjustment is accepted as a deprecated alias of jacobian. CmdStan\ModelMethods and CmdStan\StanFunctions can also be used directly with a Stan file.


Method-specific fit methods
CmdStanMCMC adds loo(variables: 'log_lik', rEff: true, momentMatch: false, maxIters: 30, kThreshold: null, split: true, cov: true) and waic(variables: 'log_lik'). Both return estimates (each with Estimate and SE), pointwise rows, and flat keys such as elpd_loo and se_elpd_loo; LOO also returns diagnostics with Pareto k values. momentMatch: true needs model methods and the phit posterior-draw kernels, and adds a moment_match key; see the inference guide.
CmdStanMLE adds mle()/optimizedParams() (final optimizer row) and lp(); its summary() returns variable/estimate rows, matching CmdStanR’s optimization summary. CmdStanVB adds variationalMean() and lpApprox(). Pathfinder and Laplace also expose lpApprox(); Laplace exposes mode(), and generated quantities fits expose fittedParamsFiles(). CmdStanPathfinder adds singlePathFiles(), singlePathJsonFiles(), singlePathFits(), and singlePathDiagnostics() for runs with save_single_paths: true. CmdStanDiagnose adds gradients() (gradient-check console output).


Statistics helpers
CmdStan\Figure renders computed figures with ascii(), vegaLite(), json(), html(), svg(), and png(); casting a figure to a string gives its ASCII form. CmdStan\Plot computes the figures, plus bandwidth(), density(), autocorrelation(), and ranks() for the values they draw. CmdStan\Psis (paretoSmooth(), paretoKhat(), psis(), gpdfit()), CmdStan\Loo (loo(), waic(), relativeEff()), CmdStan\MomentMatch (loo() on unconstrained draws with log-density and log-likelihood callbacks, fromFit()), CmdStan\DrawKernels (detection of and wrappers for the phit draw kernels), CmdStan\Summary (summarise() and each posterior measure), CmdStan\Rvars, and CmdStan\Inits (fromFit(), fromDraws(), nest(), validate()) operate on plain draws arrays. Their docblocks describe the input and output shapes.

title: API reference
section: Data frames and the phpstats family
text:
Data frames and the phpstats family
CmdStanPHP works with the phpstats family without depending on it. phibble is detected by method and class names. The phit extension is detected by function name.

Data in
Every data argument (sample(), sampleMpi(), optimize(), variational(), pathfinder(), laplace(), generateQuantities(), diagnose(), and logProb()) and write_stan_json() accept a plain array, a JSON file, a CmdStan\StanData, or a table. A table is any object with toModelData() or toColumns(), such as a phibble Phibble\DataFrame. toModelData() is used when both exist. StanData::fromTable($table, addN: true) performs the same conversion and keeps the factor labels.







Column
Stan data




int or float
The list of values, unchanged


bool
0/1 integers


list cells
Nested arrays, which must be rectangular


factor
1-based integer indices in level order, plus J_<name>, the number of levels


string
A factor with sorted unique levels (strcmp order, as phibble’s and R’s factor() defaults)


null, dates, other objects
Rejected with the column name and row, because Stan data has no missing values



Factor levels come from a toModelData() descriptor (['levels' => list<string>, 'codes' => list<?int>, 'ordered' => bool], with 0-based codes, as phibble’s DataFrame::toModelData() returns them since phibble 93858fa; add 'base' => 1 for 1-based codes) or, for a toColumns() table, from levels($name) when types() reports a factor. The ordered flag is ignored. Labels cannot be written to Stan JSON, so they are returned in StanData::$levels, keyed by data variable, where label i has index i + 1. The conversion adds N, the row count, unless the table has a column named N, and adds J_<name> unless a column already has that name. CmdStan ignores data variables that the program does not declare. Column names must be valid Stan identifiers.
Fit methods are camelCase, as are StanData‘s and Tables’ from...() constructors and the package’s other static helpers, such as CmdStanFit::fromCsv() and Inits::fromFit(). StanData is a value object with readonly data, levels, columns (the names of the columns of X), and meta. toArray() returns data, and with(['prior_scale' => 2.5]) adds or replaces variables.


Regression data
StanData::fromColumns($columns, y: 'y', x: ['x1', 'x2'], groups: 'school', intercept: false) builds the usual hierarchical regression data block from named columns or a table:







Variable
Contents




N
Number of rows


K
Number of predictors (columns of X)


X
N rows of K floats, in the order of x


y
The outcome, keeping integers as integers


<g>_id
For each grouping column g, the 1-based group index of each row


J_<g>
For each grouping column, the number of groups


J
The number of groups, when there is exactly one grouping column



Groups are numbered over sorted unique values (numbers numerically, otherwise in strcmp order) or over a factor’s levels, and the labels are in levels['<g>_id']. Predictors must be numeric. intercept: true prepends a column of ones named (Intercept). It is off by default because Stan programs usually give the intercept its own parameter.
$data = CmdStan\StanData::fromColumns($df, 'score', ['hours'], 'school');
$fit = $model->sample(data: $data, seed: 1);
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector[N] y;
  int<lower=1> J;
  array[N] int<lower=1, upper=J> school_id;
}
StanData::fromFormula('y ~ x1 + f + (1 + x1 | g)', $data, dropIntercept: false, missing: 'drop') builds regression data from an R-style formula through Phit\model_matrix() in the phit extension (phit 741d38f and later). The function handles factor predictors (treatment contrasts), interactions, transforms, and offsets, and keeps the (Intercept) column in X unless dropIntercept: true. $data can be columns, factor descriptors, or a table, whose toModelData() is passed unchanged. Without the function, fromFormula() throws a RuntimeException that names the requirement. StanData::fromModelMatrix($result) maps an existing Phit\model_matrix() result and is the only code that depends on its shape.







Formula part
Stan data




Design matrix
N (retained rows), K, and X; the column names are in columns


Numeric response
y, as integers when every value is integral, so it suits int and real declarations


Factor response
y as 0/1 for two levels (Bernoulli), or 1..C with C levels (categorical); labels in levels['y']


cbind(s, f) response
y (successes) and trials (successes plus failures)


offset()
offset


(... \| g)
<g>_id (1-based) and J_<g> per grouping factor, and J when there is one grouping factor


Random slopes, such as (1 + x \| g)
Z_<g> (N rows of the group’s columns, including the intercept column) and Q_<g>, the number of columns; omitted when every term on the group is intercept-only



Group names that are not Stan identifiers have other characters replaced by _, so the nested group g2:g1 gives g2_g1_id. Groups are numbered in factor level order when the data has descriptors or table factors, and otherwise over sorted labels (numbers numerically, otherwise byte order, as Phit\model_matrix() sorts levels). Terms on the same group are concatenated into one Z_<g>, intercept-only terms included, so (1 | g) + (0 + x | g) gives the same Z_g as (1 + x | g). Two groups whose names map to the same <g>, such as a.b and a_b, are rejected. Factors reach Phit\model_matrix() as descriptors in the data’s level order, so the first level is the reference level and a factor response is coded in that order, while plain string columns use sorted levels. missing: 'drop' removes rows with missing values in any variable the formula uses, with one E_WARNING from Phit\model_matrix(), and missing: 'raise' rejects them. The remaining result keys, including retained_rows, dropped_rows, n_input, n_dropped, terms, and assign, are kept in meta, and meta['random'][<g>] lists each group’s columns and terms.
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;          // includes the intercept column
  vector[N] y;
  int<lower=1> J;
  array[N] int<lower=1, upper=J> g_id;
  int<lower=1> Q_g;
  matrix[N, Q_g] Z_g;      // (1 + x1 | g)
}


Draws and summaries out

drawsColumns(variables: null, incWarmup: false) returns draws as columns, like posterior’s as_draws_df(): one list per variable element (such as beta[2]), then one-based .chain, .iteration, and .draw columns.
summaryColumns(variables: null, probs: [0.05, 0.95], measures: []) returns summary() as columns: variable and one column per measure.
drawsTable() and summaryTable() take the same arguments and return a Phibble\DataFrame built with DataFrame::fromColumns(). They need phpstats/phibble, which requires PHP 8.5, and throw a RuntimeException explaining this when it is not installed.
CmdStan\Tables::fromRows($rows) converts any list of associative rows, such as loo()['pointwise'], to columns.

The column arrays need no other package and suit any data frame library that accepts name-to-values columns.


Part of the phpstats family
CmdStanPHP is part of the phpstats family of PHP statistics packages:

phit: the phit native extension (Phit\ functions), which provides the moment-matching draw kernels and, when available, Phit\model_matrix().
phibble: data frames (Phibble\DataFrame).
phplyr: dplyr-style verbs for phibble tables.
phiz: a Vega-Lite grammar of graphics.

The family packages target PHP 8.5. CmdStanPHP keeps PHP 8.2 support and requires none of them.

title: API reference
text:
Errors
Invalid PHP data or options throw InvalidArgumentException. Missing files/toolchain, timeouts, and malformed CSV throw runtime errors. A nonzero command exit throws ProcessException, whose public readonly properties are command, exitCode, stdout, and stderr. A failing chain terminates other active chains; partial output files remain available for investigation. Partial outputs are not returned as a successful fit.
